correctness.rationale: For positive weights the polar factor is S and the adjacent averaging recurrence gives exact binomial convolution. With Y=J_n−n/2, on |Y|≤n/4 the Taylor segment is in [n/4,∞) at every j; the phase remainder is bounded by a constant times n^(β−2)Y², with E Y²=n/4, and the tail costs at most twice its exponentially small probability. This proves the O(n^(β−1)) linearization, in fact uniformly in j. For fixed j, n t²/8 is asymptotic to θ²β² 2^(−1−2β)n^(2β−1); the fourth-order log-cosine correction is relatively o(1), giving the three envelopes including exp(−θ²/16). Increasing unbounded phases with vanishing increments cross neighborhoods of every sufficiently large even and odd π multiple. This gives exact fixed-coordinate limsup and liminf, excludes WOT convergence at and below criticality, and yields SOT convergence above it by density and uniform boundedness. For each fixed n the far-tail n-site phase variation vanishes as j→∞ and realizes both extreme averages in the limit, giving sharp norms (including n=0). The diagonal self-commutator entries tend to zero. Sum-integral error is O(N^β) by integrating the modulus of the derivative; after substituting u=x^β, integration by parts bounds the integral by O(N^(1−β)), yielding the Cesàro mean. The replacement corrects the false nonuniform-error assertion (fixed-site damping limits, not the Taylor error, cause the quantifier issue), the tail wording, and the introductory conflation of three damping regimes with three distinct topology outcomes; the theorem and its parameter range survive unchanged.
residual_risks: The large-order replay is floating-point corroboration, not a relative-error estimate when the linearized amplitude is near zero and not proof of any infinite-dimensional claim.

value.rationale: A natural one-parameter test family separates coordinate damping from the operator norm in a known transform. The exact positive critical envelope and strong convergence with sharp norm separation are useful benchmarks: the usual regularity of adjacent weights, essential normality and a common Cesàro mean do not determine convergence. This is a precise example, not a new general transform theory.
residual_risks: No scope beyond positive weights of the given power-phase family or quantitative SOT rate on arbitrary vectors.
